During the Fall of Saigon, South Vietnamese Major Buang-Ly lands a 2 seater Cessna containing his family of 7 on the deck of the USS Midway. 1975

South Vietnamese Air Force Major Buang-Ly had loaded his family into a commandeered 2 seat Cessna and, after evading enemy fire, headed out into the South China Sea hoping to find a ship to land on. He spotted the aircraft carrier USS Midway which had been taking on evacuees from helicopters or directing aircraft to ditch in the sea and sending rescue boats for them. When a spotter reported that there were at least four people in the aircraft, thoughts of forcing the pilot to ditch alongside were abandoned as it was unlikely the passengers of the overloaded plane could survive the ditching.

After three landing attempts, Major Buang dropped a note from a low pass over the deck: "Can you move the helicopter to the other side, I can land on your runway, I can fly for one hour more, we have enough time to move. Please rescue me! Major Buang, wife and 5 child."

Admiral Lawrence Chambers issued the order to allow the plane to land. The arresting wires were removed and all helicopters that could not be relocated were pushed over the side and into the sea. To get the job done he ordered every available seaman on deck, regardless of rank.

At the time, Chambers had only been in command of the USS Midway for a few weeks and believed that his order would get him court martialed. The crew of the Midway was so impressed by Buang's skill and bravery that they established a fund to him and his family get settled in the United States. The plane is now on display at the Naval Aviation Museum in Pensacola, Florida.
